procedural_history.originating_court: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but it can be inferred that the case originated in a trial court within the jurisdiction of the Madurai Bench of Madras High Court.
procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and Order dated 10.02.2011 of the High Court of Madurai Bench of Madras in Criminal Appeal (MD) No. 519 of 2002
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The High Court of Madurai Bench of Madras heard Criminal Appeal (MD) No. 519 of 2002 and delivered a judgment and order on 10.02.2011.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The Supreme Court was approached via Criminal Appeal No. 413 of 2012 under Article 136 (Special Leave Petition) of the Constitution of India. The Supreme Court stated that it does not typically re-appreciate evidence for a third time unless there is a serious infirmity or perversity in the lower court's judgments. The Supreme Court considered the arguments, reviewed the High Court's judgment, and the materials on record, and ultimately disposed of the appeals.

decision.appeal_result: Criminal Appeal No.413 of 2012 preferred by Joseph (A11) is dismissed.
decision.conviction_status: Conviction of Sahayam (A3) and Joseph (A11) under Section 302 IPC read with Section 149 IPC is modified to Section 302 IPC read with Section 34 IPC and Section 302 IPC read with Section 109 IPC respectively. Conviction of accused Nos. 4 to 10 under Section 302 IPC read with Section 149 IPC is set aside and they are acquitted of the same. Conviction of the accused Nos. 3 to 5 under Section 148 IPC and accused Nos. 6 to 11 under Section 147 IPC are set aside.
decision.sentence_status: The sentence of life imprisonment awarded to Sahayam (A3) and Joseph (A11) is confirmed.
directions: Sahayam (A3) and Joseph (A11) are directed to surrender to serve their remaining sentence.

issue.issue_text: Whether the prosecution succeeded in proving the existence of common object amongst the accused persons and whether the accused persons acted in prosecution of the common object and that the accused persons knew that the death was likely to be committed, to convict the accused under Section 302 IPC with the aid of Section 149 IPC.

facts: An attack occurred between two factions who were attending a funeral.
Only one of the accused, A-11, had a pre-existing enmity with the victim's family.
The other accused persons acted upon the exhortation (incitement) of A-11.
law: To convict someone under Section 149 IPC (vicarious liability for an unlawful assembly), the prosecution must prove one of two things:
1. The offence was committed to accomplish the common object of the assembly (the first part of S.149).
2. The members of the assembly knew the offence was likely to be committed in the prosecution of that common object (the second part of S.149).
application: The Court found that the prosecution failed to prove that all the accused shared a common object to commit murder.
It concluded that the accused persons reacted individually to A-11's exhortation, rather than acting in furtherance of a pre-planned common goal.
Specifically for accused A-4 to A-10, the Court noted they may not have known that other accused were armed with bombs or that a murder was likely to occur.
The Court also pointed out that the High Court had not made a definite finding that the common object was murder or that the accused knew murder was a likely outcome.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court rejected the prosecution's argument, holding that it had failed to prove the existence of a common object to commit murder among all the accused. Therefore, the conviction of the accused under Section 302 IPC with the aid of Section 149 IPC could not be sustained and was modified based on their individual roles.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the prosecution succeeded in proving the existence of common object amongst the accused persons and whether the accused persons acted in prosecution of the common object and that the accused persons knew that the death was likely to be committed, to convict the accused under Section 302 IPC with the aid of Section 149 IPC.
respondent_arguments: From the evidence adduced by the prosecution and the attending circumstances of the case, the prosecution has clearly proved the existence of a common object.
The courts below rightly convicted the accused under Section 302 IPC with the aid of Section 149 IPC.

cases.case_name: Allauddin Mian and Others. Sharif Mian and Anr. v. State of Bihar
cases.principle: To fasten vicarious responsibility on a member of an unlawful assembly under Section 149 IPC, the prosecution must prove that the act was done in prosecution of the common object of that assembly or was an act the members knew to be likely to be committed. Since the section imposes constructive penal liability, it must be strictly construed.

cases.principle: For reiterating the principles of fastening vicarious responsibility on a member of an unlawful assembly under Section 149 IPC.

cases.case_name: Kuldip Yadav and Ors. v. State of Bihar
cases.principle: For reiterating the principles of fastening vicarious responsibility on a member of an unlawful assembly under Section 149 IPC.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: To establish vicarious responsibility for a member of an unlawful assembly, the prosecution must prove that the criminal act was either done in prosecution of the assembly's common object or was an act that the members knew was likely to be committed in pursuit of that object; as this section imposes constructive penal liability, it must be strictly construed.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The prosecution failed to prove the existence of a common object among the accused to commit murder, as required to invoke Section 149 IPC. The court found no evidence that all accused shared an objective to kill the deceased; rather, upon the exhortation of A11, the accused seemed to have reacted individually. Specifically, accused Nos. 4 to 10 may not have known that A1, A2, and A3 were armed with bombs, and their own actions of using sickles/sticks without targeting vital organs were inconsistent with an intent to commit murder. The High Court also failed to make a definite finding that the common object was murder or that the accused knew murder was a likely outcome.
legal_tests_applied: Section 149 IPC has two parts. The first part applies when an offence is committed in prosecution of the common object of the unlawful assembly. The second part applies when the members of the assembly had knowledge of the likelihood of the commission of that offence in prosecution of the common object.
